 O R D E R 1.
Leave granted.
2. The appellants are before this Court assailing the Order dated 14.08.2018 passed by the High Court.

A perusal of the same would disclose that the High Court essentially, has held that the acquisition has lapsed keeping in view Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 and the position of law that had been declared at that point in time.

3. The learned counsel for the appellants would point out that in fact, the appellants had brought on record the statement before the High Court to indicate that the compensation amount had been released to the Department of Land and Building amounting to a sum of Rs. 10 crores through a cheque dated 28.08.1990.
A similar issue is also arising in the connected appeals wherein, the amount is stated to have been deposited and this aspect, is also to be noted by the High Court.

The Writ Petition (C) No. 11514 of 2016, Writ Petition (C) No. 5169 of 2016 and Writ Petition (C) No. 7962 of 2016 are restored to the Board of the High Court of Delhi for reconsideration of the matter on all other issues which have been raised in the petition.

6. Since the parties are represented by their respective counsel, they may approach the Registrar of the Delhi High court to ascertain the date on which the matter would be listed before the High Court and appear without issue of fresh notice.
7. The appeals are accordingly, disposed of along with the pending application(s), if any.
